findings.title: Declared object permission check is missing on a return path
findings.description: A DRF view with an identifiable object-level policy returns lookup-derived data without an observed check on that object. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Check the same requested object using the declared object-permission policy before exposing it.

obligation.required: Check the same requested object using the declared object-permission policy before exposing it.
obligation.observed: A DRF view with an identifiable object-level policy returns lookup-derived data without an observed check on that object.
assumptions: Queryset filtering, alternate checks and deployment reachability may affect actual exposure.

findings.title: JWT signature verification is explicitly disabled
findings.description: The resolved JWT decoder explicitly sets verify_signature=False. Application authentication use and runtime library behavior require validation.
findings.recommendation: Verify signatures using a fixed, compatible algorithm/key configuration; keep unverified decoding separate from trusted claims.

obligation.required: Bind signature verification to a trusted algorithm and compatible key.
obligation.observed: The resolved JWT decoder explicitly sets verify_signature=False.
assumptions: A decode/verify call is not itself proof that its claims are used for authentication.

findings.title: HTTP chunk footer is consumed without an observed byte check
findings.description: A resolved h11 receive-buffer read supplies footer bytes whose length advances a two-byte chunk delimiter state without an observed content check. This is bounded static evidence, not verified deployment exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Validate the exact CRLF footer, including fragmented prefixes, before advancing parser state.

obligation.required: Validate the exact CRLF footer, including fragmented prefixes, before advancing parser state.
obligation.observed: A resolved h11 receive-buffer read supplies footer bytes whose length advances a two-byte chunk delimiter state without an observed content check.
assumptions: The h11 receive-buffer and chunk-event contracts identify this as HTTP/1.1 chunk framing.
